text:
support-engineer: FYI just escalated ACME SEV — EU dedicated pool p99 jumped from ~600ms to 6s around 08:45 UTC, customers seeing slow API + a handful of 504s. attaching top-line metrics and some logs :grimacing:

omar: thanks. any correlating deploys or infra changes?

support-engineer: no deploys in EU during window. billing window finished ~08:44 which usually causes a spike but this is bigger than usual. minpool for their reserved pool is 2, max 40.

leah: can you paste the autoscaler events and provisioner logs? suspecting oscillation where scaleup attempts fail and tasks queue.

support-engineer: pasted below — truncated: 
```
Provisioner: scaleup request(pool=d-ed-43, want=6) -> provisioning jobs 6
Provisioner: attach timeout 30s for gpu-attach id=az-32
Provisioner: failed attach id=az-32 err=timeout, retry
AttachController: attach rate 120/s -> throttled
Autoscaler: backoff window increased -> next attempt +5s
```

omar: attach timeout and throttling look bad. infra-bot, are we seeing image-pull or attach saturation on EU hosts?

infra-bot: [auto] image-pull errors peaked at 08:44:58 on eu-west-2, 18% pull failures; attach queue length peaked 720, avg attach time 43s. Node utilization at 92%.

leah: that explains prolonged cold GPU start. If attach queue gets big, autoscaler backs off and customer pool starves -> p99 blowup.

sara: check if model cache warmup completed — if every new node triggers a heavy model pull + quantized weights fetch can slow attach. any cache-miss spikes?

omar: metrics: model-cache-hit-rate dropped from 0.98 to 0.55 during window. so cold loads were common.

ajohnson: two immediate mitigations: 1) increase minpool to keep 6 warm GPUs for ACME for next 24h; 2) route ACME traffic to fallbacks (smaller quantized variant) until warmup finishes. thoughts?

leah: agree. Also we should proactively pre-pull the kernel image and weights on nodes used by their pool. That's a mid-term fix.

support-engineer: ACME agreed to fallbacks for next hour if we give them ETA.

omar: I'll run a manual scale action to bump minpool -> 6 for their dedicated pool id d-ed-43. doing now.

infra-bot: [auto] update accepted: pool.d-ed-43.min=6 by omar at 08:52:04 UTC. Provisioner scheduling warmup jobs.

leah: while nodes come up, let's open a short-term firewall/provisioner bypass: disable attach rate-limiter for this pool temporarily (10m window) so we don't throttle their attach retries; but we need to monitor cluster stability.

ajohnson: risky but okay if limited and monitored. set an alert to auto-revert.

omar: disabling attach-rate-limiter for d-ed-43 now.

infra-bot: [auto] attach-rate-limiter disabled for pool.d-ed-43 until 09:02:04 UTC.

support-engineer: customer reports p99 improving to ~1.2s after warmup started. still higher than baseline but much better.

leah: next actions post-mitigation:
- run root-cause check: why image-pull failures spiked (registry throttling? network flaps?)
- add proactive warmup: pre-fetch weights for heavy models during billing windows and before scheduled bursts
- review attach timeout settings and consider incremental backoff rather than fixed 30s
- add pool-specific preloaded node pools for customers with heavy SLAs

ajohnson: also add a short repro playbook for eng-oncall: steps to reproduce attach flooding in staging (script included).

leah: paste repro script in thread:
```
# repro attach storm (staging only) - run from k8s-worker w/ test creds
for i in {1..150}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging-provisioner.local/attach -d '{"pool":"d-test-1","image":"big-model:v2"}' &
done
```

leah: that'll recreate attach queue burst and model cache cold misses. use it to validate mitigations (warmup, rate-limiter adjustments, fallback routing).

omar: filing infra ticket INF-5342 for registry investigation + INF-5343 for prewarm orchestration.

support-engineer: ACME acknowledged workaround, asked for postmortem and long-term SLA proposal. I'll lock in a follow-up with CS.

ajohnson: assign owners: INF-5342 (omar), INF-5343 (leah), playbook + oncall docs (sara). I'll draft the incident timeline and mitigation summary.

sara: noted — I'll add a short runbook section in the eng-oncall repo and link from console.

omar: closing immediate action items; keeping this thread for timeline and postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [auto] thread closed for write-access but remains readable.
